sections.asr_transcript: Rotation Rotation The movement of the Earth around its own axis is called rotation. The Earth rotates from west to east. It completes one full rotation in 24 hours. The speed of rotation is faster at the equator and slower at the poles. The axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees. As the Earth is spherical in shape, only one half of the Earth receives sunlight at a time. Thus, the side of the earth facing the sun experience day. On the other hand, the other half, or the part away from the sun experiences night, as the earth rotates, the lighted part moves into the darkness. This rotation causes day and night.

Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun in a fixed path called an orbit. The Earth revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. It takes 365 and one-quarter days, one year, to complete one revolution. The tilt of the Earth's axis remains the same during revolution. Revolution causes seasonal changes. The revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis cause different seasons. summer, the hemisphere tilted towards the sun experiences summer. Winter, the hemisphere tilted away from the sun experiences winter. Spring occurs between winter and summer when the temperature starts rising. Autumn occurs between summer and winter when the temperature starts dropping.
